# fivenines_listening_ports (Data Source)

What is listening on this instance, and on which address -- where an audit or a CMDB reconciliation starts, and the one collector surface with no metric series at all.

LOOPBACK SOCKETS ARE RETURNED, flagged `loopback = true`. The dashboard hides them as noise; a data source that did the same would make "bound to loopback only" indistinguishable from "not listening", and those are opposite conclusions in a security review. Set `loopback = false` for the externally-reachable set.

These are SNAPSHOT ENTRIES, not rows: the data is a JSON array rewritten whole on every agent tick, so there is no `updated_since` cursor and no stable id -- only the natural key (port + protocol + address). Use `collector.last_reported_at` for freshness.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Everything listening, loopback sockets included and flagged
data "fivenines_listening_ports" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.web.id
}

# Only the sockets reachable off the host -- the set a security review wants
data "fivenines_listening_ports" "exposed" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.web.id
  loopback    = false
}

# protocol, address and stack are null on an agent that did not classify them,
# so keep them as attributes rather than interpolating them into a string.
output "exposed_ports" {
  value = [
    for p in data.fivenines_listening_ports.exposed.listening_ports :
    ({ port = p.port, protocol = p.protocol, address = p.address })
  ]
}

# These are snapshot entries with no timestamps, so freshness comes from the
# collector block rather than from a per-row column.
output "ports_last_reported_at" {
  value = data.fivenines_listening_ports.exposed.collector.last_reported_at
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `loopback` (Boolean) `false` returns only sockets reachable off the host -- the set a security review cares about. `true` returns only the loopback-bound ones. Omit for both.
- `protocol` (String) Exact, case-insensitive match on the transport protocol, e.g. `tcp`.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the address, protocol or port.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `listening_ports` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--listening_ports))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--listening_ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `listening_ports`

Read-Only:

- `address` (String) The address the socket is bound to.
- `loopback` (Boolean) Bound to a loopback address, so NOT reachable off the host. These entries are returned rather than hidden -- the dashboard hides them, but an API that did would make "bound to loopback only" indistinguishable from "not listening", which are opposite conclusions in a security review. Filter with `loopback=false` to get only the exposed sockets.
- `port` (Number) The port the socket is bound to. Part of the natural key (port + protocol + address); these entries carry no id.
- `protocol` (String) The transport protocol, e.g. `tcp`. Null when the agent did not classify it.
- `stack` (String) ipv4 / ipv6 / dual-stack, as the agent classified it. Null on an agent that did not.
